blogTitle: Accent Walls in Kitchens: Practical or Trendy?
videoTitle: Accent Walls in Kitchens: Practical or Trendy?
script:
Accent Walls in Kitchens: Practical or Trendy?

[warmly] You know that feeling when you walk into your kitchen and think — something's missing, but I can't quite put my finger on it? Honestly, the answer is almost always on the WALLS.

So — kitchen accent walls… are they practical, or just a trend? The honest answer is BOTH, when you pick the right material and the right wall.

Your main options are paint, tile, shiplap, wallpaper, or stone — and each one has its own personality… and its own rules for the kitchen.

A little tip I love: whatever material you go for — always check it's RATED for kitchen use, so it can handle humidity, grease, and temperature changes near the hob.

Now — choosing the RIGHT wall… this is where most people trip up. Your best accent wall is the one your eye naturally falls on the moment you walk into the room.

Think about SIGHTLINES — the wall behind the hob, the end of a galley, or the wall opposite your main window… those are usually your best candidates.

[curious] Okay, colour — this is the fun bit… Deep forest green, warm terracotta, inky navy… any of these on one kitchen wall can completely REFRAME the whole room.

And for paint — always go satin or semi-gloss finish in a kitchen… flat paints look gorgeous in living rooms, but they're a NIGHTMARE near a hob, trust me.

Budget vs high-end… paint is the most affordable and reversible option — but tile and stone give you that really LUXURIOUS, durable result if you want to invest a bit more.

Here's a quick breakdown — paint and brick slips sit at the budget-friendly end… wallpaper and shiplap are mid-range… and natural stone or full tile work is your high-end investment.

Once your accent wall is in place, styling AROUND it is everything — think open shelving, a few considered ceramics, maybe a trailing plant… let the wall breathe.

[excited] And wall art on or near your accent wall? That's honestly one of my favourite finishing touches — it pulls the whole colour story together beautifully.

Small kitchen? One well-chosen accent wall can actually make the space feel BIGGER — especially a lighter colour or a subtle texture rather than something dark and busy.

If you've got an open-plan kitchen-diner, your accent wall needs to work ACROSS both spaces — same colour story, same energy… so the two areas feel like they belong together.

Wall art is such a brilliant way to complement a kitchen accent wall… and prints that echo the room's palette — food, botanicals, travel — feel RIGHT at home in a kitchen.

Like this — the Coffee Shop Wall Design set of three prints… warm, illustrated, and they sit beautifully against a painted or tiled accent wall without competing with it.

Or if Italian lifestyle is your thing… this set of three Italian prints is honestly one of my favourites — that warm Mediterranean energy works SO well in a kitchen.

Renters — good news… peel-and-stick wallpaper, removable tile stickers, and picture rails mean you can absolutely CREATE an accent wall effect without touching a single thing permanently.

And here's another gorgeous Italian lifestyle gallery wall set — perfect for renters who want IMPACT without commitment… just frame them, hang them, done.

Before you start — there's a simple planning checklist worth running through: pick your wall, choose your material, check kitchen suitability, then think about how the WHOLE room will style around it.

[sighs] The styles worth knowing right now… dark and moody painted walls, raw brick slips, bold geometric tile, and warm shiplap… each one totally different but all completely brilliant done right.

And for some visual inspiration — this Italian lifestyle set brings in that soft, sun-drenched warmth that works BEAUTIFULLY as a gallery wall against almost any accent finish.

Design experts all say the same thing — a kitchen accent wall doesn't need to be DRAMATIC to be effective… it just needs to be intentional. That's the whole secret, really.

And finally — this last Italian gallery wall set… it's the kind of thing that takes a plain kitchen wall and turns it into something that actually feels like PART of your home.

Did you know styling your home doesn't have to be guesswork?

From colour theory and design principles to gallery wall layouts and art sizing. Download them all from our site!

Find all you need to transform your home into a calming oasis!

Happy Decorating!

A set of three framed botanical prints in muted sage and cream tones hang centrally on the accent wall, perfectly echoing the green palette. A person stands at the kitchen island, coffee mug in hand, glancing warmly toward the feature wall — the room feels lived-in, considered, and genuinely aspirational.
